haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts one nightly run. It extracts rows from the replica with updated_at later than hwm minus 2 hours, including deleted orders.
haiku-low.q2: The brief says bulk-import rows can become visible up to 90 minutes after their updated_at, so the 2-hour lookback covers that window.
haiku-low.q3: The next nightly extract picks it up, since its updated_at is after the lookback start. The merge replaces the stored row because the newer updated_at wins.
haiku-low.q4: The order is kept in fact_orders with is_deleted set to true. Deleted orders are never removed from the warehouse.
haiku-low.q5: A failed row is written to etl_runs with the error text. The run waits 15 minutes and retries from Extract, up to three attempts. After attempt 3 fails, it pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous night's data, never a partial load. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts when no nightly success row exists.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. Its row count and checksum comparison finds the mismatch for that order's creation day, and it reloads that whole day from the replica.
haiku-low.q8: A stored row is replaced only when the staged updated_at is equal or later. So an older or duplicate copy changes nothing.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl_watermark. It is set to the largest updated_at in staging, in the same transaction as the merge, only when the merge succeeds.
haiku-low.q10: The merge and the hwm move commit in one transaction. A failure rolls everything back, so dashboards see either the new night or the previous one.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is emptied at the start of the retry, so the failed attempt's staged rows are discarded. The retry extracts again from the unchanged hwm minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every order created that day from the replica and upserts them with the latest-updated_at-wins and is_deleted rules. It does not move the hwm.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts one nightly run at 02:00 UTC. Extract reads from the replica every order with updated_at later than (hwm minus 2 hours), deleted orders included.
sonnet.q2: Bulk-import rows can become visible on the replica up to 90 minutes after their updated_at (the document gives no reason beyond that).
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a newer updated_at, so a later nightly extract (updated_at after hwm minus 2h) picks it up and the merge upserts it, replacing the stored row because the staged updated_at is equal or later.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (and updates updated_at). The next extract picks it up, the merge upserts it and sets is_deleted true. The row stays in fact_orders; nothing is hard-deleted.
sonnet.q5: Merge rolls back if it failed, and the hwm and warehouse are unchanged. A failed row with the error text is written to etl_runs. The run waits 15 minutes and restarts at Extract. Up to 3 attempts; if attempt 3 fails, on-call is paged and nothing re-runs automatically.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous night's data (never a partial load). The 06:00 check finds no nightly success row and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation: it compares row count and checksum per order-creation day for the last 30 days against the replica, finds the mismatch, and reloads that whole day (upsert), which brings in the version.
sonnet.q8: The upsert replaces a stored row only when the staged updated_at is equal or later, so older copies never overwrite newer ones and a repeated copy changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: In the etl_watermark table in the warehouse. The value is the largest updated_at in staging (unchanged if staging is empty). It is written inside the Merge transaction, at commit together with the upsert and the success row.
sonnet.q10: The merge, the hwm move and the success row commit in one warehouse transaction, so fact_orders shows either the new night or the previous one. Dashboards also never read stg_orders.
sonnet.q11: Staging is emptied at the start of the retry's Extract, so the failed attempt's staged rows are discarded. The hwm did not move, so the retry extracts the same window: updated_at later than hwm minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads every order created that day from the replica, empties stg_orders, and merges them in one transaction using the step 3 upsert and is_deleted rules. It skips the watermark part, so the hwm does not move. It writes its own etl_runs row marked as a reload.
